name: Correlative Conjunction Pairs
description: Analyzes the frequency and strict syntactic symmetry of paired correlative conjunctions (e.g., 'not only... but also', 'either... or').
mechanism: Large Language Models are rigorously trained to output grammatically flawless text. One of the hallmarks of this perfectionism is the aggressive use of formal correlative conjunctions, such as 'not only [X] but also [Y]', 'neither [X] nor [Y]', or 'both [X] and [Y]'. Crucially, the AI executes these pairings with mathematically perfect syntactic symmetry—ensuring that the grammatical structure immediately following 'not only' perfectly matches the structure following 'but also'. Human writers, outside of strict academic or professional editing, use these formal pairs less frequently and often commit parallel structure errors when they do (e.g., 'not only verbs... but also nouns'). This method extracts these correlative pairs and calculates their density and internal parallel symmetry. A high frequency of flawless correlative structures points to an algorithmic generator prioritizing textbook grammar over natural variance.
useCase: Identifying artificially eloquent essays, marketing copy, and formal articles that lean heavily on textbook-perfect correlative grammar to sound authoritative.
strengths:
• Highly effective on 'persuasive' or 'analytical' AI prompts where the model attempts to compare or aggregate concepts formally.
• Evaluates deep syntactic symmetry, making it completely immune to simple word spinners or synonym replacement.
• Leverages human imperfection; parallel structure errors are common in humans but virtually non-existent in modern LLMs.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when evaluating highly edited human text, such as published journalism, legal documents, or academic papers.
• Completely ineffective on short-form text or casual dialogue where correlative pairings are naturally absent regardless of the author.
• Easily bypassed by explicitly instructing the AI to use informal, broken grammar or conversational tone.
parameters:
Analysis: Correlative Conjunction Extraction & Dependency Parsing
Metric: Pair Density & Syntactic Parallelism
Output: 0-100 Correlative Formalism Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85%. Particularly lethal on generated B2B marketing, persuasive essays, or analytical comparisons. Useless on casual or fictional text.

references.title: Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
